data.title: Product Roadmap
data.tagline: A dynamic plan that communicates product goals, priorities, and expected outcomes across time horizons
data.learningOutcome: You can organize a roadmap around goals, expected outcomes, and time horizons, then distinguish it from a product backlog, PRD, and Gantt chart.
data.description: A trip product might use Now for reliable saving, Next for collaborative editing, and Later for testing automatic planning. A roadmap communicates direction and tradeoffs; distant work rarely supports exact date commitments.

learning.assumes: You have seen quarterly feature lists that do not explain goals or distinguish forecasts from commitments.
learning.outcome: You can organize a roadmap around goals, expected outcomes, and time horizons, then distinguish it from a product backlog, PRD, and Gantt chart.

explanation.title: Start with goals and user outcomes
explanation.text: State the problem and desired result before listing the work that may support it.

explanation.title: Use horizons to preserve flexibility
explanation.text: Near-term work can be clearer; distant work uses broader horizons and changes with evidence.

explanation.title: Make daily work traceable
explanation.text: Connect roadmap direction to the Product Backlog and specific requirements.

data.boundary: A Product Roadmap explains direction, a Product Backlog orders candidate work, and a Gantt Chart schedules selected tasks. A roadmap horizon is not automatically a delivery commitment.

lessonPractice.title: Which plan is closest to a product roadmap?

options.label: Now: reduce lost itineraries; Next: support co-editing; Later: validate demand for automatic planning, with an expected user outcome for each horizon
options.feedback: Correct. It uses time horizons to communicate goals, direction, and expected outcomes while leaving distant work adjustable.

options.label: List the exact file each developer will edit every day for six weeks, with hourly completion times
options.feedback: That is task scheduling. It answers who does what and when, not how the product should evolve.

options.label: Put every suggested feature into a list without goals, order, or time horizons
options.feedback: An unordered wish list cannot communicate product direction or tradeoffs.

data.agentPrompt: Using these confirmed product goals, user evidence, and constraints, create a Now–Next–Later product roadmap. For each horizon, state the problem, expected user outcome, and candidate work. Mark unsupported features and dates as open questions. Explain major tradeoffs and dependencies without turning distant horizons into fixed commitments or daily task schedules.
